feature1.prompt: PK setup for MTI to parent gets confused by multiple OneToOne references. In a multi‐table inheritance scenario, when a model (for example, Picking inheriting from Document) defines more than one OneToOneField, the ordering of these fields can lead to the wrong field being used as the parent link. In the problematic case, defining the field with parent_link=True after another OneToOneField causes an ImproperlyConfigured error. The fix should ensure that only the OneToOneField with the explicit parent_link marker is considered for setting up the primary key and parent link, regardless of its position in the class.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves adjusting the logic for identifying OneToOneField instances with parent_link in the model base. Developers should focus on modifying the loop in django/db/models/base.py so that the field is only processed if field.remote_field.parent_link is true. This change must ignore other OneToOneFields that do not have the explicit parent_link marker. The solution should ensure that the ordering of field definitions is no longer a factor in determining the proper parent link.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/base.py – Locate the __new__ method where local_fields are iterated. Modify the condition that currently checks for isinstance(field, OneToOneField) so that it also verifies field.remote_field.parent_link is true.

feature2.prompt: PK setup for MTI to parent gets confused by multiple OneToOne references. In certain model definitions, the absence of an explicit parent_link on a OneToOneField (as seen in the Picking model) causes an ImproperlyConfigured error with the message 'Add parent_link=True to appname.Picking.origin.' Although reordering the fields can sometimes work, this error indicates that the check for parent_link is too strict. The intended fix is to remove the check that forces a OneToOneField to have parent_link=True, so that only fields with an explicit parent_link marker are used in establishing the parent connection.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature requires removing the check in the model options that raises an ImproperlyConfigured exception when a OneToOneField is missing the parent_link attribute. Developers should update django/db/models/options.py by eliminating the code block that raises the exception if field.remote_field.parent_link is not true. The modification must ensure that the configuration and validation logic remain consistent with the updated field identification in the model base.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/options.py – In the _prepare method, remove the check that raises ImproperlyConfigured if a OneToOneField does not have parent_link=True, and update the import to no longer include ImproperlyConfigured.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Files django/db/models/base.py and django/db/models/options.py, along with the model inheritance configuration and associated test modules.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 will expose the updated API for field identification in model inheritance while Feature2 will remove the redundant validation check. Both features must be integrated so that the base logic and the options validation remain consistent. Integration tests should be run to ensure that models are correctly recognized without triggering ImproperlyConfigured errors.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers on Feature1 and Feature2 should coordinate to confirm that the new OneToOneField identification logic in base.py is fully aligned with the relaxed validation in options.py. Regular code reviews and joint integration testing sessions are recommended.
